name: Somerville
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Somerville, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Somerville, MA: Santa on a fire truck at the City Hall tree lighting, lantern-making workshops, the Lantern Parade and Illuminations.
lede: Somerville's holidays mix the traditional and the homemade: Santa rolling up to City Hall on a red fire truck, a brand new Lantern Parade with free workshops to build your own lantern, and porches lit up across the city for Illuminations.
celebrates: The City of Somerville publishes a full holiday schedule each year. It opens with the Christmas Tree Lighting on the City Hall Concourse, where Santa makes a grand entrance on a red fire truck and children receive gifts. The schedule also lists a menorah lighting, a self-guided Illuminations map of decorated homes, Festivus at Statue Park, Three Kings Day and holiday gift drives, and it closes with the flag raising on Prospect Hill on New Year's Day. The Somerville Arts Council adds the first Somerville Lantern Parade along the Community Path to Davis Square, with free lantern-making workshops led by artist Bonny Chen beforehand.
lastyear: In 2025 the City of Somerville held its Annual Christmas Tree Lighting Ceremony on Thursday, December 4, on the City Hall Concourse, with Mayor Katjana Ballantyne inviting residents to join her. The year before, the lighting fell on Thursday, December 5, at 5 pm. The tradition goes back many years: under an earlier mayor the city followed the lighting with a meet and greet with Santa in the Somerville High School Highlander Cafe.
facts: Somerville was settled as part of Charlestown, became its own town on March 3, 1842, and incorporated as a city in 1872. A report for the Somerville Historical Society called the name purely fanciful. On January 1, 1776, the Grand Union Flag was raised on Prospect Hill during the Siege of Boston, and the National Park Service notes that the city hoists it again on Prospect Hill every January 1.
trains: Railroads shaped Somerville. The Fitchburg Railroad was built in 1841 alongside today's Somerville Avenue and began passenger service in 1843, and at its height the city had eight passenger rail stations. Today the MBTA Fitchburg Line stops at Porter, just over the line in Cambridge, one stop from North Station. For a holiday train ride, Edaville in Carver runs a train through the Christmas lights, and the Boston Street Railway Association keeps the region's trolley history alive.

kidfact: On New Year's Day in 1776, soldiers raised one of the first American flags on Prospect Hill in Somerville. Every January 1 the city raises the same kind of flag there again.
faq: When is the Somerville tree lighting?

The City of Somerville holds its Christmas Tree Lighting on a Thursday evening in early December on the City Hall Concourse at 93 Highland Avenue. In 2025 it was on December 4. Santa arrives on a red fire truck, then stays for visits and photos, and the city lists the event as free.
What is the Somerville Lantern Parade?

The Lantern Parade is a new Somerville Arts Council event, a walk with handmade lanterns along the Community Path from Cedar Street to Statue Park in Davis Square. The Arts Council will not hand out lanterns, so it runs free lantern-making workshops beforehand, led by Somerville artist Bonny Chen.

Illuminations is Somerville's season of decorated homes. The city shares a self-guided map so families can walk or drive past houses and porches lit up for the holidays. The Somerville Arts Council has also run Illuminations tours in past years.
Can we take the train to Somerville?

Somerville's closest commuter rail stop is Porter on the MBTA Fitchburg Line, just over the line in Cambridge and one stop from North Station. The Fitchburg Railroad first ran along Somerville Avenue in the 1840s, and the city once had eight passenger rail stations.
